mainEntity.name: Should I hire a bookkeeper or a CPA first?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually a bookkeeper first — to keep your day-to-day records accurate. Your CPA handles tax filing and strategy, which is far easier and cheaper when the books are already clean.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between a bookkeeper and a controller?

acceptedAnswer.text: A bookkeeper records transactions and reconciles accounts. A controller owns the accuracy of the whole financial picture — the close, reporting, controls, and what the numbers mean.

mainEntity.name: When is it time to hire help for my books?

acceptedAnswer.text: When bookkeeping eats real time, you're falling behind, volume has climbed, you've added employees, you can't answer basic financial questions, or something big (loan, sale, audit) is coming.

mainEntity.name: Do I have to hire someone full-time?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Fractional and outsourced bookkeeping, controller, and CFO services let you buy exactly the level of help you need.
